description: Test your knowledge of Ventricular System & Special sensory pathways.

cards.text: Describe the four parts of each lateral ventricle and how they communicate with the 3rd ventricle.
cards.answer: The four parts are anterior horn (frontal lobe), body (parietal), posterior horn (occipital), and inferior horn (temporal). They communicate with the 3rd ventricle via the foramen of Monro (interventricular foramen).

tip.tip: ABPI — Anterior, Body, Posterior, Inferior. Foramen of Monro = gateway between lateral and 3rd ventricles.

cards.text: Name the three CSF exits from the 4th ventricle into the subarachnoid space.
cards.answer: Foramen of Magendie (median aperture into cisterna magna) and two foramina of Luschka (lateral apertures into pontine cistern).

cards.text: In aqueductal stenosis, which ventricles dilate and which remain normal-sized?
cards.answer: Lateral and 3rd ventricles dilate because CSF cannot flow through the stenosed aqueduct of Sylvius. The 4th ventricle remains normal-sized.

tip.tip: Stenosis = bottleneck. Ventricles BEFORE the block enlarge; those AFTER are spared.

cards.text: How does Dandy-Walker malformation differ from aqueductal stenosis in ventricular involvement?
cards.answer: In Dandy-Walker, ALL four ventricles dilate due to failure of foramina of Magendie and Luschka to open. In aqueductal stenosis, the 4th ventricle is spared.

tip.tip: Dandy-Walker = ALL ventricles enlarged. Aqueductal stenosis = 4th ventricle escapes.

cards.text: A child has occipital headaches worse on coughing and cerebellar tonsils 6 mm below the foramen magnum. What is the diagnosis?
cards.answer: Chiari malformation Type I. Tonsillar descent >5 mm blocks CSF circulation at the foramen magnum, causing communicating hydrocephalus and syringomyelia.

tip.tip: Chiari = Cerebellar descent. Classic: occipital headache worsening with Valsalva (coughing/straining).

cards.text: At the optic chiasm, which retinal fibres decussate and what visual field do they represent?
cards.answer: Nasal retinal fibres (representing the temporal visual field) decussate. Temporal retinal fibres (representing the nasal visual field) remain ipsilateral.

tip.tip: Nasal crosses; Temporal stays. Opposite halves of visual field cross to opposite sides of brain.

cards.text: Compare VP shunt and ETV for treating congenital hydrocephalus in terms of mechanism and clinical use.
cards.answer: VP shunt diverts CSF from ventricle to peritoneal cavity using a valve but requires revision as the child grows. ETV creates a fenestration in the 3rd ventricle floor; preferred in older children because it avoids implanted hardware.

tip.tip: VP shunt = hardware (needs revisions). ETV = opening (no hardware to replace, preferred for aqueductal stenosis).
